content: Julie gets to drafting the collected ideas and notes into a proposal for Finn to share
"and who will do the checking? people who also want their issues addressed? No. the tide of opinions will forever divide the nation to the point of mutual hatred."
"Politics doesn't work on a binary so there will be a multitude of positions and solutions anyway. Why constrict ourself to parties."

"You see, all people with power can't just let things happen without their thoughts being projected, which is what has really bothered me. Having a way to make sure all being are at the same power and same mindset allows for a more confident and honest debate. donation controls and voting controls would help prevent this. Along with keeping gods and these wardens outside the system, and if they do want to, have to do it as if they are like the rest of us."
"Because you need numbers to affect change."

Finn looks to <@339235123759153162>

"Andross, if I may still call you by this name, you hold a unique position and have experience of being abused by people in power in this city. You have heard many other ideas today but I haven't heard where your heart sways now."
"This is why the opinion of the people matter. The needs of the many will always out weigh the few and everyone's voice is important."
A halfling pipes up. "Why can't we just share everything? Money is whats keeping serfs down. If everyone is equal, why do we have really rich people and really poor people."
"The government type Finn suggested would be good in solving issues of economic inequality, I think."
"Yes, Finn did bring good point to these"
"But. why should one person own a farm, or shovel? We could all help!" says the halfling. "Ownership is super selfish."

"As it stands, I am happy with none of the outlines of government that we started with, but with the voices of people here, the Midaskian choice would help address inequalities, expand quality of life, as well as make sure decisions represent the interests of the people."

He looks to Julie
"How's my proposal looking so far, did you get the bit about the council earning minimum wage?"
Julie looks up and pushes up her glasses and nods before furiously going back to writing

"To reiterate the big picture of it: 
- Term Limits on all positions
- Representative and proportional elections
- Welfare programs to take care of extreme class divisions, inequalities and great privileges
- Individualism and Free Will including speech, assembly, beliefs, life choices!

Most importantly, checks making sure public servants in elected positions stay just that. No profiting from a position of power. Having them make the minimum wage of the country and be dedicated to bettering the lives of the people they represent!"
"We can improve on what others have attempted. Let us not make a carbon copy of history"
"The minimum wage should be a living wage, too."
5 goblins enter the building and take a seat on the balcony.

"But doesn't having a position of power held by multiple people mean that they will still benefit from being in power? Not financial (which is terrible idea. Good leadership should be incentivizing) they will still be able to change policies at their whim. They way life is done could be flipped upside down from committee to committee."
The minutaur bellows.
"Thats why we set rules now. Rights they cannot take away from us. We create limits to their power."

"Policy change would be in the bodies of congress, not from the executive branch. Their decisions would be in the suggestion of new policy ratified by congressional approval. Their entire job would be enforcing the laws set and appointing the cabinet of experts instead of changing the government infrastructure"
"Does not your congress change it's members?"
"Term limits would enforce it so, but those members would be representative of the people of the nation"
"Also laws and taxes put in place that were set without a vote of the people should be able to be refused by a vote of the people"

"Poppy cock. They all have their own motivations. For the length of their term they will be 'trusted' by the people who voted. There can't be a way of regulating how they will act and what their feelings would be."
"And illegal or not, pleanty of people who want power will figure out a way to trade it to those who lobby them for specifc issues, regarless of if they come from the people of their homeland"
"That's the neat part, there is a way of regulating them!"
"That's kind of the basis of the idea"
"What if those who want to trade power simply take the money after the term?"

"So what are you suggesting  then? No leader?" Vivica looks annoyed "Everyone has their own agenda but limits to power will keep them from overstepping their boundaries. They won't be above the law either. All of which we have been saying this whole time."
"No! The beast person at the job should get the job. And the best leaders are the ones we already have. Why the titans of industry of course."
Vivica rolls her eyes at that comment. "The best leaders are those people rally behind."
Nolan shakes his head to this, mimicking others’ voices. “Leaders of industry often think of money before people.”

"Surely those who merit power by proving their abilities in the private sector have already accomplished a ralleying of people. Those of us at vanderbilt can afford to gift everyone in this room with 10,000 gold. Because we are already successful."
"I wouldn't rally behind a leader just because I work for them. A job is a job but this is the livelihood of a nation being born."
"Vanderbilt, it's the 1,800 cases for abuse and exploitation in your company that steer most people away from that idea of government"
"Oh yes. The livelyhood. Imagine a world that could pay for your toil and provide the things you need all at the same time."
“All people deserve life, liberty, and the pursuit happiness, regardless of wealth or social standing. And the people at the bottom deserve a voice as much as those glittering with gold.”
Vivica sits back and listens to what others have to say, tired of the arguments being made. ( <@264570136025890816> feel free to puppet me to share your voice so you don't have to mimic everything.)
A human sized mantis person and a hippo person wearing some weird uniform walk in and sit to watch.

"i live by creed. people get what they work for. and if anyone has an issue one way or another it gets decided as people decide. I'm for warden sworn monarchs to ensure fair reward for honest labor and sacrifices. and should  that monarch or any official he makes seem like they are unfit a person who believes themself qualified can throw their hat in and challenge for the position. we all need each other to build and live, that sorts itself out when everyone is pushed to earn their keep. and those that can't can still  live at peace when good hearts help them out since we're basing a lot of this on people being good hearted."

"Instead of having leaders and government based on meritocratic choices, why not leave that to the economic system for incentives? Hardworking individuals like yourself get compensated more for the jobs they do in the private sector, while these fulfill public servant positions that don't allow the amassing of power. The ability to challenge someone's power would be inherent in majority votes of no confidence or in reelection years when they are either given another term, or removed from office"
"let me ask you this. what do we need out of our leadership. what do they do?"
"To inform policy on infrastructure, security, resource allocation, inhabit the ideals and values of the people, increase the general welfare of the public, and so on"
“To enact the will of the people and to protect them.”
Finn takes over the writing of his drafted idea from Julie and fills in some more items

"then why not simply make them a judge instead of authority? people can rally themselves for wars, revolution, business and so on. That's all we need. The burden of sustaining oneself is to themselves and one is always welcome and encouraged to help a brother or sister who struggles."

"Because then it leaves those unable to perform to profitable standards without any means in which to adequately live. Having a system to ensure domestic welfare programs would be more effective than solely leaving people to help one another. This way, there could be both"

"we always need thinkers, workers, and leaders. and this is nothing about profit, this is about community. the farmer needs farmhands, builders hardly work alone, and workers need leaders, artists need inspiration, and everyone needs philosophers to keep everyone thinking."
"this isn't about letting everyone grow, this is about getting by. when it gets competitive of peoples own choices then you can police profits."

"really the only thing we need is a frame of currency to base labor. then we have the standard for how a leader is meant to judge. gives us a value for any imports of what we'd like to have from other nations. 'profits' are just fancy talk for people like him." he points a rude finger to Vanderbilt

"Sure, we could create a system where everyone has full freedom to keep to themselves and only has their livelihood affected when crime or judgement by an elected judge is needed, but it misses the values of the system we have organically created in siblinghood. We can do better by having a system that works together to have everyone's lives promoted better than they had it. A compliment to community in the form of public welfare and democracy"

"can a system truly capture a creed? when we talk 'life, liberty, pursuit of happiness' or 'basic needs' we had that as colonies. you needed a house, you built it. you need food, you grow it. if you couldn't do it yourself you ask your neighbor. government WILL complicate it and ruin that with imposing on others, which can get twisted whether intended or not."

"This may have been the way that villages in ancient times or rural areas did it, but we live in a daring city that we collectively empower to band together. Execution will come down to the elected candidates, but we can certainly make great strides in capturing the ideals we set forth when we first declared independence"
bones sits back and puffs his pipe. "it's a pick your poison no matter how you slice it, you can only make leaps of faith that whatever you pick works. nothing is forever."
"And I severely hope that the system we put into place is not its final form by the end, that would be the true shame. This will need to be amended as times, values, and needs change too"
"Which is better? Ethics or morality?" Posses Cassie the old woman.
"While Ethics is a group consensus of right and wrong and eventually becomes the law of the land, laws can me misinterpreted. They can be bent or loop holed, or broken in secret."

"Morality is what the individual defines as right and wrong. Which is what we have here. We have a discussion of morality which will be a compromised average of ideas and feelings. None of us has the same morality, yet here we are deciding in. The ethics to become law. There ought to be a single standard of what is wrong and what is right. Something that gets is all on the same page. For what kind of backwards logic is it to rely that one person believe it is fine to eat of the flesh of a sentient being, while other s practice cannibalism with out a care in the world. Not. If we are to start with morality, there should be a Moral standard set by a being who has proven themselves to be above reproach in their dealing with us. Thr wardens ought to be the moral law givers, by way of a high priest or priestess. And that should also become the ethics."

"You made me think of something. The way we define justice, what should that look like in this nation? I think if we take a restorative approach as opposed to a punitive we would be able to build stronger communities. Not only does restorative measures follow many indigenous practices and forms of justice but it also seeks to prevent repeat offenders. People will learn the consequences of their actions without having to be cycled through the system over and over."

Paul revere holding a lantern which sheds the same light as the lamplighter's lights enters the building. With him is and animated flag (the flag of roanoke) in the shape of a dwarf with ta long brimmed hat, he is wearing a massive backpack that takes up two seats. The crowed waiting at the back take their seats after he does.
"That should get its own Article moreso than how the Justice system is organized"
He takes an extra paper and begins writing down some ideas
Seeing that she has not been heard. Cassie. Has left the front to sit with the crowd at the back.
Vivica opens her own notebook and writes down some ideas as well mumbling some idea for how the justice system should function

A white leonin takes the soap box. "What of the ability to protect one's self. And who will control the military. And what of the banks? Which currency shall we use? I propose a gold standard and notes that may be redeemed. There is more than enough gold out west to back it. "

"That would be a fair idea backed with credit powers as well. The idea is that wherever among our states we go, we would only pay a single currency. Using this standard would allow us to repurpose the British coinage to our own."
"Must we all look at king georges ugly mug on every coin?" The dwarf made of flag asks loudly. There is a chuckle throughout the room.
"No no, as in we melt it down"
"Print our own using the resources"
"We can of course change the images on the coin, though that is a later matter for after we've established our government, I think."
Ben Franklin joins the balcony. A pretty redheaded gentlethey in tow.
The mender gives a polite nod to Mr Franklin
Finn gives a friendly wave and gets back to drafting up his proposal
Ben Franklin shouts. "I proclaim that the national animal that represents us be the glorious turkey."

"We keep talking about power and how to restrict it, clearly no one wants to deal with someone like this so-called King back in England. While we all have different ideas of morality and of who should lead and how, no one should be able to overstep. Thomas Jefferson once said 'In questions of power, then, let no more be heard of confidence of a person, but bind them down from mischief by the chains of the Constitution.'
"A constitution that we will create here and now."
"Here here! And for the Turkey, I don't know, I think a  Platypus-Bear would be more appealing, those suckers can swim faster than sharks!"
Some one calls out "awena the owlbear!" (It is season 1 cannon that the first winged owlbear cub will one day be on the currency of Arcania.)
Lili smiles.

the Mender stands once more "I have heard it said a chain is only as strong as its weakest link.  The more people that run the government.... the more chances of a weak link.  I feel that many of you are forgetting something very important.... there have been countless monarchs that did right by their people.... that rules just and fair.  We don't talk about them because they did as they were supposed to.... no one wastes breath on the ordinary.... only the extraordinary cases... the cases where the monarch did wrong.  I bet none here can list more than a couple handfuls of bad monarchs, out of the tens of thousands that have run this world.  You are sitting here trying to guess the best method of preventing abuse of power.... abuses against peoples lives... liberty... and happiness.  A well placed sword or poison will do more to stop tyranny than laws.... laws that can be manipulated.... laws that can be ignored.... laws that can be changed.... or worse yet laws that cannot be changed.  Seek someone wise... someone compassionate... someone that cares... someone that looks to a better tomorrow.  Don't seek a perfect person... seek a person that will do right by the people, and trust the people will keep them in line.... You are foolish to depend on group consensus.  It slows everything down, and gives voice to the uninformed.... it allows jesters to set policy...." he shakes his head "Look to Ben Franklin as your leader.  Someone that seeks not war.... but seeks a better tomorrow.  Someone that has not devoted his life to death... but to making a better life for everyone.  Everyone is dancing around the core issue.... what is best of the people.  The people in this room are making decisions that impact the people outside these walls.  The people that live in our lakes.... burrow under out soil.... and as much as I hate to bring them up.... fly in our air.  You make decisions for people born of this land.... and those seeking refuge... from today... til, gods and wardens willing, the end of time.  Don't give the people a weak chain easily broken by politics.... give them a good person, a wise leader, one that will do right by them... Instead of a chain.... you give them an unbreakable rod.  I am sure that such a good person... the people will find ways of extending their lives til a suitable replacement can be found."
He sits, and chews a goodberry

Finn stands up from his seat to address it

"Although I do not believe the ratio of good to bad monarchs is as you say it is, I believe it detracts from the foundation this nation was to be built with. One of our first grievances taken with King George and ratified in our declaration among many others was the taxation without representation, the lack of agency or ability to stop the quartering of troops in our homes. King George gave us a puppet delicate that would share our words on his deaf ears and they met with naught. We are not some nation made out of a vacuum. We are a nation of people that have been abused and oppressed by the monarchy system and stripped of our free will to do otherwise until we decided to fight for liberty and justice for all. Putting the power to form, bend, or remove law in the hands of a single person or small group would be detrimental to the vast people we are forming this government to represent."
"A good foundation is where we must begin. We can seek someone wise, and someone compassionate but as Eliza said earlier, power corrupts and we must place limits to that power."

"So a Declaration made out of fear and earnest is the deciding factor that an intellectual and wise body of people are hoping to use as a foundation?  A declaration of war is the foundation you wish to build a new country on?  A cornerstone of fear and war will only lead to fear and war.  Maybe the problem is leaning on the crutch of the declaration of war as the foundation.  The problem is not a monarch... the problem is the monarch in question."

"Agreed. Absolute power corrupts absolutely. No, not a declaration of war. A Declaration of Independence, that we are freed people, not under the rule of a king or emperor. It is a document of hope that we place our will in"
"A well-instructed people alone can be permanently a free people' a quote from James Madison. We will educate our people, all people in this new nation and they will set the standard for freedom."
